title: The Word That Changed Its Address
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空例。実在の人物・調査結果・史料・収蔵品ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A word can remain familiar to speakers of a language even after the circumstances in which it is commonly used have changed.
sentences.ja: 一般的に使用される状況が変化した後でも語は言語話者に身近なままであり得る。

sentences.en: Someone reading a letter written by an earlier generation may therefore recognize nearly every word without immediately understanding the writer's intended message.
sentences.ja: 以前の世代の手紙を読む人はほぼ全語を認識しても筆者の意図したメッセージをすぐ理解しないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The difficulty may come not from an unfamiliar spelling but from a familiar expression whose meaning depends on a different social context.
sentences.ja: 困難は未知の綴りでなく意味が異なる社会文脈に依存する身近な表現から生じ得る。

sentences.en: This possibility is illustrated by an imaginary exchange between two members of the same family.
sentences.ja: この可能性は同一家族の二人の架空のやり取りで示される。

sentences.en: A grandmother shows her grandson a collection of letters that she received from friends during her school years.
sentences.ja: 祖母は学生時代に友人から受け取った手紙集を孫に見せる。

sentences.en: He notices an expression that he normally encounters in humorous messages exchanged among his classmates.
sentences.ja: 普段級友間のユーモラスなメッセージで出会う表現に気づく。

sentences.en: When he reads the expression aloud, he assumes that the original writer was trying to make his grandmother laugh.
sentences.ja: 声に出して読むと元の筆者が祖母を笑わせようとしていたと想定する。

sentences.en: She explains, however, that the expression was generally understood among her friends as a sincere way to communicate admiration.
sentences.ja: しかし友人間では称賛を伝える誠実な方法として一般に理解されていたと説明する。

sentences.en: The grandson begins comparing the contexts in which the expression appears, rather than searching for a single dictionary definition that would explain every instance of its use.
sentences.ja: 全使用例を説明する辞書定義一つを探すのでなく表現が出る文脈を比較し始める。

sentences.en: He notices differences in the relationships between writers and readers, the occasions that encouraged them to communicate, and the other expressions appearing nearby.
sentences.ja: 書き手と読み手の関係、伝達を促した機会、付近の他表現の違いに気づく。

sentences.en: His grandmother also points out that her own memories cannot establish how every speaker of the language understood the expression during the same period.
sentences.ja: 祖母は自身の記憶が同時期の全話者の理解を確定できないとも指摘する。

sentences.en: Together they distinguish evidence about a particular community of speakers from a universal claim about the language as a whole.
sentences.ja: 二人は特定話者集団についての根拠と言語全体についての普遍的主張を区別する。

sentences.en: For a school project, the grandson prepares an imaginary collection of examples that illustrates how an expression could acquire different associations in different circumstances.
sentences.ja: 学校活動で表現が異なる事情で異なる連想を得る様子を示す架空の例集を作る。

sentences.en: He labels the examples according to their intended contexts so that readers do not mistake them for genuine historical documents.
sentences.ja: 読者が本物の歴史文書と誤認しないよう想定文脈に従って例にラベルを付ける。

sentences.en: The project encourages his classmates to consider why someone might misunderstand a familiar expression despite recognizing its individual words.
sentences.ja: 活動は個々の語を認識しても身近な表現を誤解し得る理由を級友に考えさせる。

sentences.en: It also allows them to discuss how meaning may develop within a community without requiring every speaker to adopt the same interpretation.
sentences.ja: 全話者に同じ解釈を採用させず共同体内で意味がどう発展するか議論できるようにする。

sentences.en: Language is not simply a collection of words whose meanings can always be separated from the situations in which people use them.
sentences.ja: 言語は意味を使用状況から常に切り離せる単なる語の集合ではない。

sentences.en: A familiar word may carry associations that reflect the experiences of a particular group or period.
sentences.ja: 身近な語は特定集団や時期の経験を反映する連想を持つかもしれない。

sentences.en: Understanding an earlier text sometimes requires examining those associations rather than assuming that the most familiar present-day interpretation must also apply to the past.
sentences.ja: 過去の文章の理解には最も身近な現代解釈が過去にも適用されると想定せず連想を調べる必要がある場合がある。

sentences.en: The imaginary letter serves as a reminder that recognizing a word and understanding its use are related but distinct achievements.
sentences.ja: 架空の手紙は語の認識と使用の理解が関連するが別個の達成であることを思い出させる。

questions.prompt: Why may a familiar word be difficult to interpret in an old letter?
options: Earlier generations used no recognizable words.
Every word has exactly one meaning.
Its earlier social context may be different.

questions.prompt: What example does the text introduce?
questions.explanation_ja: 架空の家族のやり取り。

questions.prompt: How does the grandson initially interpret the expression?
options: As an attempt to make someone laugh.
As an expression of sincere admiration.
As a request for financial assistance.

questions.prompt: How did the grandmother's friends understand it?
options: As a criticism of the reader.
As a sincere expression of admiration.

questions.prompt: Why examine contexts rather than one definition?
options: Usage and relationships may influence meaning.
Every context must produce the same meaning.

questions.prompt: What limitation does the grandmother acknowledge?
options: Her letters are all modern messages.
Her memories cannot represent every speaker.
questions.explanation_ja: 個人記憶の一般化は不可。

questions.prompt: Why does the grandson label the examples?
options: To guarantee a correct answer in every case.
To prevent fictional examples being mistaken for historical documents.

questions.prompt: What can classmates learn from the project?
options: Recognition of words does not guarantee understanding of their use.
Every speaker should adopt one interpretation.
Older texts should always be read humorously.
Understanding words requires attention to their changing social associations and contexts.
Personal memories establish universal language rules.
